14"""metax-private ``torch.linalg.qr`` (``aten::linalg_qr``). 

15 

16The generic implementation (``flag_gems.ops.linalg_qr``) is tuned for NVIDIA 

17H20 and is fully correct there. This backend override compensates for three 

18metax (MACA) platform quirks, each verified in isolation on the hardware: 

19 

201. **fp64 ``tl.dot`` returns garbage** (deterministically wrong values, all 

21 tile shapes / warp counts; fp32 dot is exact). Kernels that use ``tl.dot`` 

22 on the fp64 code paths get dot-free copies here 

23 (``_larft_kernel_mx`` / ``_larfb_kernel_mx`` / ``_tsqr_apply_kernel_mx``), 

24 with the matrix products computed as row-chunked broadcast (rank-CH) 

25 updates -- verified to ~1e-16 vs CPU references. fp32 keeps ``tl.dot`` 

26 everywhere. 

272. **The fused multi-panel Q-assembly kernel miscompiles** (same class of 

28 failure as the iluvatar override): ``_assemble_q_fused_kernel``'s single 

29 launch does identity + reverse panel loop with cross-iteration global 

30 write->read of Q, and returns a wrong Q on this backend. Q assembly uses 

31 the stream-ordered variant (identity kernel + one larfb per panel), so 

32 every cross-panel dependency is ordered by the stream. All other generic 

33 pieces (fused small-matrix path, TSQR local/tree kernels, geqrt panels) 

34 are verified correct here and reused as-is. 

353. **64 KB shared memory per CTA** (H20: 228 KB) and ~128 KB of private 

36 (register) tile budget. The two limits bite different kernels, so the 

37 tile caps are recalibrated from on-hardware measurements 

38 (``_GEQRT_SRAM_MAX_M``, the ``_TSQR_MX_*`` budgets below); the 

39 H20-calibrated caps raise ``OutOfResources`` (or spill) at kernel launch. 

40 

41Structure: this module is SELF-CONTAINED -- it never mutates the generic 

42module. Generic kernels / helpers that are correct on this backend are 

43imported and launched directly; the fp64-broken or miscalibrated pieces get 

44``*_mx`` variants here, and the top-level routing (``_linalg_qr_mx``) mirrors 

45the generic ``_linalg_qr`` with those variants plugged in. Only 

46``float32`` / ``float64`` are supported, matching the generic op. 

47""" 

48

103# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

104# dot-free matrix helpers (fp64 tl.dot is broken on this backend -- see #1) 

105# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

106@triton.jit 

107def _mm_row_col(A, B, dt, M: tl.constexpr, K: tl.constexpr, N: tl.constexpr): 

108 """C[m, n] = sum_k A[m, k] * B[k, n] via outer-product accumulation. 

109 

110 ``A`` is (M, K), ``B`` is (K, N); ``K`` serial steps of a rank-1 update. 

111 Only used on fp64 paths (small K = a panel / block width); fp32 keeps 

112 ``tl.dot``, which is exact on this backend. 

113 """ 

114 ki = tl.arange(0, K) 

115 zero = tl.full((), 0.0, dtype=dt) 

116 C = tl.zeros((M, N), dtype=dt) 

117 for k in range(K): 

118 ak = tl.sum(tl.where(ki[None, :] == k, A, zero), axis=1) # A[:, k] 

119 bk = tl.sum(tl.where(ki[:, None] == k, B, zero), axis=0) # B[k, :] 

120 C += ak[:, None] * bk[None, :] 

121 return C 

122

124# =========================================================================== 

125# dot-free variant of the generic _larft_kernel (fp64 only; fp32 routes to 

126# the generic kernel, whose tl.dot is exact here). The Gram matrix is built 

127# with row-chunked broadcast products (rank-CH updates) instead of tl.dot or 

128# the O(K^2) extraction loop: optimal M*ib^2 work. 

129# =========================================================================== 

130@libentry() 

131@triton.jit 

132def _larft_kernel_mx( 

133 V, 

134 TAU, 

135 MOUT, 

136 M, 

137 ib, 

138 sVb, 

139 sVm, 

140 sVn, 

141 sTauB, 

142 sTauN, 

143 sMb, 

144 sMm, 

145 sMn, 

146 RM: tl.constexpr, # unused (kept for launch-signature parity) 

147 IBN: tl.constexpr, 

148 CH: tl.constexpr, 

149): 

150 pid = tle.program_id(0) 

151 Vb = V + pid * sVb 

152 TAUb = TAU + pid * sTauB 

153 Tb = MOUT + pid * sMb 

154 

155 dt = Vb.dtype.element_ty 

156 idx = tl.arange(0, IBN) # row/col index 0..IBN-1 

157 

158 # ---- Gram G = V^H V (IBN x IBN), rank-CH broadcast updates ---- 

159 # (CH, IBN, IBN) fp64 broadcast tile: CH=4, IBN=64 -> 32 KB registers 

160 G = tl.zeros((IBN, IBN), dtype=dt) 

161 for t in range(0, (M + CH - 1) // CH): 

162 rows = t * CH + tl.arange(0, CH) 

163 rmask = rows < M 

164 v_off = rows[:, None] * sVm + idx[None, :] * sVn 

165 Vc = tl.load(Vb + v_off, mask=rmask[:, None] & (idx[None, :] < ib), other=0.0) 

166 G += tl.sum(Vc[:, :, None] * Vc[:, None, :], axis=0) 

167 

168 # ---- M = T^{-1} = triu(G, 1) + diag(1/tau) (upper triangular) ---- 

169 tau_vec = tl.load(TAUb + idx * sTauN, mask=idx < ib, other=1.0) 

170 inv_tau = tl.where(tau_vec != 0.0, 1.0 / tau_vec, float("inf")) 

171 Mmat = tl.where(idx[:, None] < idx[None, :], G, 0.0) 

172 Mmat = tl.where(idx[:, None] == idx[None, :], inv_tau[:, None], Mmat) 

173 

174 # fp64 stores M = T^{-1}; the fp64 larfb solves against it (SOLVE path) 

175 out = Mmat 

176 

177 tl.store( 

178 Tb + idx[:, None] * sMm + idx[None, :] * sMn, 

179 out, 

180 mask=(idx[:, None] < ib) & (idx[None, :] < ib), 

181 ) 

182 

183 

184# =========================================================================== 

185# dot-free variant of the generic _larfb_kernel (fp64 only; fp32 routes to 

186# the generic kernel). Both products (W1 = V^H C and C -= V Y) are 

187# row-chunked broadcast reductions -- optimal M*ib*TN work, no fp64 tl.dot, 

188# no O(K^2) extraction loop. Y comes from the in-kernel triangular solve on 

189# M=T^{-1} (SOLVE path), as in the generic fp64 kernel. 

190# =========================================================================== 

191@triton.jit 

192def _larfb_kernel_mx( 

193 V, 

194 TOUT, 

195 C, 

196 M, 

197 ib, 

198 P, 

199 sVb, 

200 sVm, 

201 sVn, 

202 sTb, 

203 sTm, 

204 sTn, 

205 sCb, 

206 sCm, 

207 sCn, 

208 RM: tl.constexpr, 

209 IBN: tl.constexpr, 

210 TN: tl.constexpr, 

211 UPPER: tl.constexpr, 

212 SOLVE: tl.constexpr, 

213 CH: tl.constexpr, 

214): 

215 pid_b = tle.program_id(0) 

216 pid_p = tle.program_id(1) 

217 Vb = V + pid_b * sVb 

218 Tb = TOUT + pid_b * sTb 

219 Cb = C + pid_b * sCb 

220 

221 dt = Cb.dtype.element_ty 

222 col_idx = tl.arange(0, IBN) 

223 p_idx = pid_p * TN + tl.arange(0, TN) 

224 pmask = p_idx < P 

225 

226 Msram = tl.load( 

227 Tb + col_idx[:, None] * sTm + col_idx[None, :] * sTn, 

228 mask=(col_idx[:, None] < ib) & (col_idx[None, :] < ib), 

229 other=0.0, 

230 ) 

231 

232 # ---- W1 = V^H C[:, p-tile] (rank-CH broadcast updates) ---- 

233 # (CH, IBN, TN) fp64 broadcast tile: CH=4, IBN=64, TN=32 -> 64 KB regs 

234 W1 = tl.zeros((IBN, TN), dtype=dt) 

235 for t in range(0, (M + CH - 1) // CH): 

236 rows = t * CH + tl.arange(0, CH) 

237 rmask = rows < M 

238 v_off = rows[:, None] * sVm + col_idx[None, :] * sVn 

239 c_off = rows[:, None] * sCm + p_idx[None, :] * sCn 

240 Vc = tl.load( 

241 Vb + v_off, mask=rmask[:, None] & (col_idx[None, :] < ib), other=0.0 

242 ) 

243 Cc = tl.load(Cb + c_off, mask=rmask[:, None] & pmask[None, :], other=0.0) 

244 W1 += tl.sum(Vc[:, :, None] * Cc[:, None, :], axis=0) 

245 W1 = tl.where(col_idx[:, None] < ib, W1, 0.0) 

246 

247 # ---- Y: triangular solve on M = T^{-1} (SOLVE path) ---- 

248 Y = tl.zeros((IBN, TN), dtype=dt) 

249 if UPPER: 

250 for jj in range(IBN): 

251 i = IBN - 1 - jj 

252 if i < ib: 

253 Mrow = tl.sum(tl.where(col_idx[:, None] == i, Msram, 0.0), axis=0) 

254 W1row = tl.sum(tl.where(col_idx[:, None] == i, W1, 0.0), axis=0) 

255 Mii = tl.sum(tl.where(col_idx == i, Mrow, 0.0)) 

256 contrib = tl.sum( 

257 tl.where(col_idx[:, None] > i, Mrow[:, None] * Y, 0.0), axis=0 

258 ) 

259 Yrow = (W1row - contrib) * (1.0 / Mii) 

260 Y = tl.where(col_idx[:, None] == i, Yrow[None, :], Y) 

261 else: 

262 for i in range(IBN): 

263 if i < ib: 

264 Mcol = tl.sum(tl.where(col_idx[None, :] == i, Msram, 0.0), axis=1) 

265 W1row = tl.sum(tl.where(col_idx[:, None] == i, W1, 0.0), axis=0) 

266 Mii = tl.sum(tl.where(col_idx == i, Mcol, 0.0)) 

267 contrib = tl.sum( 

268 tl.where(col_idx[:, None] < i, Mcol[:, None] * Y, 0.0), axis=0 

269 ) 

270 Yrow = (W1row - contrib) * (1.0 / Mii) 

271 Y = tl.where(col_idx[:, None] == i, Yrow[None, :], Y) 

272 Y = tl.where(col_idx[:, None] < ib, Y, 0.0) 

273 

274 # ---- C[:, p-tile] -= V Y (rank-CH broadcast updates) ---- 

275 for t in range(0, (M + CH - 1) // CH): 

276 rows = t * CH + tl.arange(0, CH) 

277 rmask = rows < M 

278 v_off = rows[:, None] * sVm + col_idx[None, :] * sVn 

279 c_off = rows[:, None] * sCm + p_idx[None, :] * sCn 

280 Vc = tl.load( 

281 Vb + v_off, mask=rmask[:, None] & (col_idx[None, :] < ib), other=0.0 

282 ) 

283 Cc = tl.load(Cb + c_off, mask=rmask[:, None] & pmask[None, :], other=0.0) 

284 Cc = Cc - tl.sum(Vc[:, :, None] * Y[None, :, :], axis=1) 

285 tl.store(Cb + c_off, Cc, mask=rmask[:, None] & pmask[None, :]) 

286 

287 

288# =========================================================================== 

289# dot-free variant of the generic _tsqr_apply_kernel. Only the products on 

290# the fp64 path change: the final Q = X @ Qti and the two-level composition 

291# Qti = Qti @ Qt2i. The FOLD_TREE branch is fp32-only by routing and keeps 

292# its selection dot. 

293# =========================================================================== 

294@libentry() 

295@triton.jit 

296def _tsqr_apply_kernel_mx( 

297 V_local, 

298 TAU_local, 

299 Qt, 

300 Qt2, 

301 Q, 

302 Rblocks, 

303 Racc, 

304 m, 

305 n, 

306 br, 

307 k_max, 

308 grp, 

309 num_blocks, 

310 sQb, 

311 sQm, 

312 sQn, 

313 sRAb, 

314 sRAm, 

315 sRAn, 

316 BM: tl.constexpr, 

317 IBN: tl.constexpr, 

318 TWO_LEVEL: tl.constexpr, 

319 FOLD_TREE: tl.constexpr, 

320 BRMt: tl.constexpr, 

321 NO_DOT: tl.constexpr, 

322): 

323 pid_b = tle.program_id(0) 

324 block_id = tle.program_id(1) 

325 Vb = V_local + pid_b * (m * n) 

326 TAUb = TAU_local + pid_b * (num_blocks * n) + block_id * n 

327 stack_batch = num_blocks * n * n 

328 

329 dt = Vb.dtype.element_ty 

330 zero = tl.full((), 0.0, dtype=dt) 

331 one = tl.full((), 1.0, dtype=dt) 

332 

333 rm = tl.arange(0, BM) 

334 cn = tl.arange(0, IBN) 

335 blk_start = block_id * br 

336 M = tl.minimum(br, m - blk_start) 

337 nr = tl.minimum(k_max, M) 

338 rmask = rm < M 

339 cmask = cn < n 

340 

341 Vt = tl.load( 

342 Vb + (blk_start + rm)[:, None] * n + cn[None, :], 

343 mask=rmask[:, None] & cmask[None, :], 

344 other=zero, 

345 ) 

346 tau_vec = tl.load(TAUb + cn, mask=cn < nr, other=zero) 

347 

348 # Q_local = H_0 ... H_{nr-1} [I; 0] (reverse order application) 

349 X = tl.where(rm[:, None] == cn[None, :], one, zero) 

350 for jj in range(nr): 

351 j = nr - 1 - jj 

352 vj = tl.sum(tl.where(cn[None, :] == j, Vt, zero), axis=1) 

353 tau_j = tl.sum(tl.where(cn == j, tau_vec, zero)) 

354 w = tau_j * tl.sum(vj[:, None] * X, axis=0) 

355 X = X - vj[:, None] * w[None, :] 

356 

357 cq = tl.arange(0, IBN) 

358 if FOLD_TREE: 

359 # (fp32-only branch, unchanged from the generic kernel) 

360 rt = tl.arange(0, BRMt) 

361 Rm_t = num_blocks * n 

362 gmask = rt < Rm_t 

363 G = tl.load( 

364 Rblocks + pid_b * stack_batch + rt[:, None] * n + cn[None, :], 

365 mask=gmask[:, None] & cmask[None, :], 

366 other=zero, 

367 ) 

368 taut = tl.zeros([IBN], dtype=dt) 

369 for j in range(n): 

370 col_j = tl.sum(tl.where(cn[None, :] == j, G, zero), axis=1) 

371 alpha = tl.sum(tl.where(rt == j, col_j, zero)) 

372 xnorm_sq = tl.sum(tl.where(rt > j, col_j * col_j, zero)) 

373 norm = tl.sqrt(alpha * alpha + xnorm_sq) 

374 beta = tl.where(alpha >= zero, -norm, norm) 

375 reflect = xnorm_sq > zero 

376 beta_eff = tl.where(reflect, beta, alpha) 

377 tau = tl.where(reflect, (beta - alpha) / beta, zero) 

378 denom = alpha - beta 

379 v_tail = tl.where(reflect, col_j / denom, zero) # guard 0/0 NaN 

380 G = tl.where((rt[:, None] == j) & (cn[None, :] == j), beta_eff, G) 

381 G = tl.where((rt[:, None] > j) & (cn[None, :] == j), v_tail[:, None], G) 

382 taut = tl.where(cn == j, tau, taut) 

383 vj = tl.where(rt > j, v_tail, tl.where(rt == j, one, zero)) 

384 pmask = cn[None, :] > j 

385 w = tau * tl.sum(tl.where(pmask, vj[:, None] * G, zero), axis=0) 

386 G = tl.where(pmask, G - vj[:, None] * w[None, :], G) 

387 if block_id == 0: 

388 R_tile = tl.where(rt[:, None] <= cn[None, :], G, zero) 

389 tl.store( 

390 Racc + pid_b * sRAb + rt[:, None] * sRAm + cn[None, :] * sRAn, 

391 R_tile, 

392 mask=(rt[:, None] < n) & cmask[None, :], 

393 ) 

394 Xt = tl.where(rt[:, None] == cn[None, :], one, zero) 

395 for jj in range(n): 

396 j = n - 1 - jj 

397 v_tail = tl.sum(tl.where(cn[None, :] == j, G, zero), axis=1) 

398 vj = tl.where(rt > j, v_tail, tl.where(rt == j, one, zero)) 

399 tau_j = tl.sum(tl.where(cn == j, taut, zero)) 

400 w = tau_j * tl.sum(vj[:, None] * Xt, axis=0) 

401 Xt = Xt - vj[:, None] * w[None, :] 

402 S = tl.where(rt[None, :] == (block_id * n + cq)[:, None], one, zero) 

403 Qti = tl.dot(S, Xt, allow_tf32=False) 

404 Qti = tl.where(cq[:, None] < n, Qti, zero) 

405 else: 

406 Qti = tl.load( 

407 Qt + pid_b * stack_batch + (block_id * n + cq)[:, None] * n + cn[None, :], 

408 mask=(cq[:, None] < n) & cmask[None, :], 

409 other=zero, 

410 ) 

411 if TWO_LEVEL: 

412 # compose with the group rows of the top-level factor first 

413 gid = block_id // grp 

414 num_groups = (num_blocks + grp - 1) // grp 

415 Qt2i = tl.load( 

416 Qt2 

417 + pid_b * (num_groups * n * n) 

418 + (gid * n + cq)[:, None] * n 

419 + cn[None, :], 

420 mask=(cq[:, None] < n) & cmask[None, :], 

421 other=zero, 

422 ) 

423 if NO_DOT: 

424 Qti = _mm_row_col(Qti, Qt2i, dt, IBN, IBN, IBN) 

425 else: 

426 Qti = tl.dot(Qti, Qt2i, allow_tf32=False) 

427 if NO_DOT: 

428 out = _mm_row_col(X, Qti, dt, BM, IBN, IBN) 

429 else: 

430 out = tl.dot(X, Qti, allow_tf32=False) 

431 tl.store( 

432 Q + pid_b * sQb + (blk_start + rm)[:, None] * sQm + cn[None, :] * sQn, 

433 out, 

434 mask=rmask[:, None] & cmask[None, :], 

435 ) 

436

438# =========================================================================== 

439# dot-free variant of the generic _assemble_q_single_panel_kernel (fp64). 

440# Single panel (k <= ib): Q = I - V T V^H, with W1 = T V[p,:]^H read straight 

441# off V's rows and each output tile written exactly once. T is stored as 

442# M = T^{-1} on the fp64 path, so W1 comes from the same in-kernel 

443# upper-triangular solve as _larfb_kernel_mx; the V_t @ W1 product uses the 

444# outer-product extraction loop (fp64 tl.dot is broken here). 

445# =========================================================================== 

446@libentry() 

447@triton.jit 

448def _assemble_q_single_panel_kernel_mx( 

449 V, 

450 T, 

451 Q, 

452 m, 

453 k, 

454 qcols, 

455 sVb, 

456 sVm, 

457 sVn, 

458 sTb, 

459 sTm, 

460 sTn, 

461 sQb, 

462 sQm, 

463 sQn, 

464 RM: tl.constexpr, 

465 TN: tl.constexpr, 

466 IBN: tl.constexpr, 

467): 

468 pid_b = tle.program_id(0) 

469 pid_r = tle.program_id(1) 

470 pid_p = tle.program_id(2) 

471 Vb = V + pid_b * sVb 

472 Tb = T + pid_b * sTb 

473 Qb = Q + pid_b * sQb 

474 

475 dt = Qb.dtype.element_ty 

476 zero = tl.zeros((), dtype=dt) 

477 one = tl.full((), 1.0, dtype=dt) 

478 col_idx = tl.arange(0, IBN) # padded reflector columns 

479 p_idx = pid_p * TN + tl.arange(0, TN) # Q columns of this CTA 

480 pmask = p_idx < qcols 

481 rm = tl.arange(0, RM) 

482 

483 # Z = V[p_idx, :k]^H (IBN, TN); masks use k (reflectors), not n 

484 Vrows = tl.load( 

485 Vb + p_idx[:, None] * sVm + col_idx[None, :] * sVn, 

486 mask=(p_idx[:, None] < m) & (col_idx[None, :] < k), 

487 other=zero, 

488 ) 

489 Z = tl.trans(Vrows) 

490 # M = T^{-1} (upper triangular, IBN x IBN) 

491 Msram = tl.load( 

492 Tb + col_idx[:, None] * sTm + col_idx[None, :] * sTn, 

493 mask=(col_idx[:, None] < k) & (col_idx[None, :] < k), 

494 other=zero, 

495 ) 

496 

497 # W1 = T @ Z <=> solve M W1 = Z by back substitution. Every row-tile 

498 # CTA redundantly solves for W1 (k serial steps on an (IBN, TN) tile) -- 

499 # cheap next to the row-parallel Q write it buys, and rows/tau beyond k 

500 # are exactly zero (Mii=+inf convention as in _larfb_kernel_mx). 

501 W1 = tl.zeros((IBN, TN), dtype=dt) 

502 for jj in range(k): 

503 i = k - 1 - jj 

504 Mrow = tl.sum(tl.where(col_idx[:, None] == i, Msram, 0.0), axis=0) 

505 Zrow = tl.sum(tl.where(col_idx[:, None] == i, Z, 0.0), axis=0) 

506 Mii = tl.sum(tl.where(col_idx == i, Mrow, 0.0)) 

507 contrib = tl.sum( 

508 tl.where(col_idx[:, None] > i, Mrow[:, None] * W1, 0.0), axis=0 

509 ) 

510 W1row = (Zrow - contrib) * (1.0 / Mii) 

511 W1 = tl.where(col_idx[:, None] == i, W1row[None, :], W1) 

512 W1 = tl.where(col_idx[:, None] < k, W1, zero) 

513 

514 # Q_tile = I_tile - V_t @ W1, written once; one row tile per CTA 

515 # (outer-product loop runs k steps, not IBN -- k << IBN for narrow panels) 

516 rows = pid_r * RM + rm 

517 rmask = rows < m 

518 Vt = tl.load( 

519 Vb + rows[:, None] * sVm + col_idx[None, :] * sVn, 

520 mask=rmask[:, None] & (col_idx[None, :] < k), 

521 other=zero, 

522 ) 

523 Qt = tl.where(rows[:, None] == p_idx[None, :], one, zero) 

524 ki = tl.arange(0, IBN) 

525 for kk in range(k): 

526 ak = tl.sum(tl.where(ki[None, :] == kk, Vt, zero), axis=1) 

527 bk = tl.sum(tl.where(ki[:, None] == kk, W1, zero), axis=0) 

528 Qt -= ak[:, None] * bk[None, :] 

529 tl.store( 

530 Qb + rows[:, None] * sQm + p_idx[None, :] * sQn, 

531 Qt, 

532 mask=rmask[:, None] & pmask[None, :], 

533 ) 

534 

535 

536# =========================================================================== 

537# Row-parallel fp64 larft/larfb for tall panels. The dot-free serial kernels 

538# above loop over ALL M panel rows per CTA (larft: one CTA per batch; larfb: 

539# one CTA per column tile), which costs ~2.7/5.3 ms per panel at m=4096. For 

540# M > _PAR_GRAN the row reductions are split across RB = ceil(M/_PAR_GRAN) 

541# row-chunk CTAs that write partial tiles; a second, stream-ordered launch 

542# reduces the partials (fixed order -> deterministic, no atomics, no 

543# cross-CTA barriers) and finishes the panel. 

544# =========================================================================== 

545@libentry() 

546@triton.jit 

547def _larft_gram_partial_kernel_mx( 

548 V, 

549 Gpart, 

550 M, 

551 ib, 

552 sVb, 

553 sVm, 

554 sVn, 

555 sGb, 

556 sGr, 

557 sGm, 

558 sGn, 

559 GRAN: tl.constexpr, 

560 IBN: tl.constexpr, 

561 CH: tl.constexpr, 

562): 

563 """Partial Gram of one GRAN-row chunk of V: G_r = V[lo:hi]^H V[lo:hi].""" 

564 pid = tle.program_id(0) 

565 rid = tle.program_id(1) 

566 Vb = V + pid * sVb 

567 Gb = Gpart + pid * sGb + rid * sGr 

568 

569 dt = Vb.dtype.element_ty 

570 idx = tl.arange(0, IBN) 

571 lo = rid * GRAN 

572 hi = tl.minimum(lo + GRAN, M) 

573 

574 G = tl.zeros((IBN, IBN), dtype=dt) 

575 for t in range(0, (hi - lo + CH - 1) // CH): 

576 rows = lo + t * CH + tl.arange(0, CH) 

577 rmask = rows < hi 

578 v_off = rows[:, None] * sVm + idx[None, :] * sVn 

579 Vc = tl.load(Vb + v_off, mask=rmask[:, None] & (idx[None, :] < ib), other=0.0) 

580 G += tl.sum(Vc[:, :, None] * Vc[:, None, :], axis=0) 

581 # columns >= ib are exactly zero (Vc masked), so an unmasked store is safe 

582 tl.store(Gb + idx[:, None] * sGm + idx[None, :] * sGn, G) 

583 

584 

585@libentry() 

586@triton.jit 

587def _larft_finalize_kernel_mx( 

588 Gpart, 

589 TAU, 

590 MOUT, 

591 RB, 

592 ib, 

593 sGb, 

594 sGr, 

595 sGm, 

596 sGn, 

597 sTauB, 

598 sTauN, 

599 sMb, 

600 sMm, 

601 sMn, 

602 IBN: tl.constexpr, 

603): 

604 """G = sum_r G_r; M = T^{-1} = triu(G, 1) + diag(1/tau) (as _larft_kernel_mx).""" 

605 pid = tle.program_id(0) 

606 Gb = Gpart + pid * sGb 

607 TAUb = TAU + pid * sTauB 

608 Tb = MOUT + pid * sMb 

609 

610 dt = TAUb.dtype.element_ty 

611 idx = tl.arange(0, IBN) 

612 

613 G = tl.zeros((IBN, IBN), dtype=dt) 

614 for r in range(RB): 

615 G += tl.load(Gb + r * sGr + idx[:, None] * sGm + idx[None, :] * sGn) 

616 

617 tau_vec = tl.load(TAUb + idx * sTauN, mask=idx < ib, other=1.0) 

618 inv_tau = tl.where(tau_vec != 0.0, 1.0 / tau_vec, float("inf")) 

619 Mmat = tl.where(idx[:, None] < idx[None, :], G, 0.0) 

620 Mmat = tl.where(idx[:, None] == idx[None, :], inv_tau[:, None], Mmat) 

621 tl.store( 

622 Tb + idx[:, None] * sMm + idx[None, :] * sMn, 

623 Mmat, 

624 mask=(idx[:, None] < ib) & (idx[None, :] < ib), 

625 ) 

626 

627 

628@libentry() 

629@triton.jit 

630def _larfb_w1_partial_kernel_mx( 

631 V, 

632 C, 

633 Wpart, 

634 M, 

635 ib, 

636 P, 

637 sVb, 

638 sVm, 

639 sVn, 

640 sCb, 

641 sCm, 

642 sCn, 

643 sWb, 

644 sWr, 

645 sWp, 

646 sWm, 

647 sWn, 

648 GRAN: tl.constexpr, 

649 IBN: tl.constexpr, 

650 TN: tl.constexpr, 

651 CH: tl.constexpr, 

652): 

653 """Partial W1_r = V[lo:hi]^H C[lo:hi, p-tile] for one row chunk.""" 

654 pid_b = tle.program_id(0) 

655 rid = tle.program_id(1) 

656 pid_p = tle.program_id(2) 

657 Vb = V + pid_b * sVb 

658 Cb = C + pid_b * sCb 

659 

660 dt = Cb.dtype.element_ty 

661 col_idx = tl.arange(0, IBN) 

662 tn_idx = tl.arange(0, TN) 

663 p_idx = pid_p * TN + tn_idx 

664 pmask = p_idx < P 

665 lo = rid * GRAN 

666 hi = tl.minimum(lo + GRAN, M) 

667 

668 W1 = tl.zeros((IBN, TN), dtype=dt) 

669 for t in range(0, (hi - lo + CH - 1) // CH): 

670 rows = lo + t * CH + tl.arange(0, CH) 

671 rmask = rows < hi 

672 v_off = rows[:, None] * sVm + col_idx[None, :] * sVn 

673 c_off = rows[:, None] * sCm + p_idx[None, :] * sCn 

674 Vc = tl.load( 

675 Vb + v_off, mask=rmask[:, None] & (col_idx[None, :] < ib), other=0.0 

676 ) 

677 Cc = tl.load(Cb + c_off, mask=rmask[:, None] & pmask[None, :], other=0.0) 

678 W1 += tl.sum(Vc[:, :, None] * Cc[:, None, :], axis=0) 

679 Wb = Wpart + pid_b * sWb + rid * sWr + pid_p * sWp 

680 tl.store(Wb + col_idx[:, None] * sWm + tn_idx[None, :] * sWn, W1) 

681 

682 

683@libentry() 

684@triton.jit 

685def _larfb_solve_kernel_mx( 

686 TOUT, 

687 Wpart, 

688 Yout, 

689 RB, 

690 ib, 

691 P, 

692 sTb, 

693 sTm, 

694 sTn, 

695 sWb, 

696 sWr, 

697 sWp, 

698 sWm, 

699 sWn, 

700 sYb, 

701 sYp, 

702 sYm, 

703 sYn, 

704 IBN: tl.constexpr, 

705 TN: tl.constexpr, 

706 UPPER: tl.constexpr, 

707): 

708 """Y = M\\W1 per (batch, p-tile): reduces the RB row-chunk partials into 

709 W1 and runs the serial triangular solve on M = T^{-1} exactly once 

710 (convention of _larfb_kernel_mx). Hoisting this out of the apply kernel 

711 removes the per-(row-chunk, p-tile) redundant partial re-reads (up to 

712 RB*IBN*TN elements per CTA) and repeated k-step solves.""" 

713 pid_b = tle.program_id(0) 

714 pid_p = tle.program_id(1) 

715 Tb = TOUT + pid_b * sTb 

716 

717 dt = Tb.dtype.element_ty 

718 col_idx = tl.arange(0, IBN) 

719 tn_idx = tl.arange(0, TN) 

720 

721 Wb = Wpart + pid_b * sWb + pid_p * sWp 

722 W1 = tl.zeros((IBN, TN), dtype=dt) 

723 for r in range(RB): 

724 W1 += tl.load(Wb + r * sWr + col_idx[:, None] * sWm + tn_idx[None, :] * sWn) 

725 W1 = tl.where(col_idx[:, None] < ib, W1, 0.0) 

726 

727 Msram = tl.load( 

728 Tb + col_idx[:, None] * sTm + col_idx[None, :] * sTn, 

729 mask=(col_idx[:, None] < ib) & (col_idx[None, :] < ib), 

730 other=0.0, 

731 ) 

732 

733 # ---- Y: triangular solve on M = T^{-1} (same as _larfb_kernel_mx) ---- 

734 Y = tl.zeros((IBN, TN), dtype=dt) 

735 if UPPER: 

736 for jj in range(IBN): 

737 i = IBN - 1 - jj 

738 if i < ib: 

739 Mrow = tl.sum(tl.where(col_idx[:, None] == i, Msram, 0.0), axis=0) 

740 W1row = tl.sum(tl.where(col_idx[:, None] == i, W1, 0.0), axis=0) 

741 Mii = tl.sum(tl.where(col_idx == i, Mrow, 0.0)) 

742 contrib = tl.sum( 

743 tl.where(col_idx[:, None] > i, Mrow[:, None] * Y, 0.0), axis=0 

744 ) 

745 Yrow = (W1row - contrib) * (1.0 / Mii) 

746 Y = tl.where(col_idx[:, None] == i, Yrow[None, :], Y) 

747 else: 

748 for i in range(IBN): 

749 if i < ib: 

750 Mcol = tl.sum(tl.where(col_idx[None, :] == i, Msram, 0.0), axis=1) 

751 W1row = tl.sum(tl.where(col_idx[:, None] == i, W1, 0.0), axis=0) 

752 Mii = tl.sum(tl.where(col_idx == i, Mcol, 0.0)) 

753 contrib = tl.sum( 

754 tl.where(col_idx[:, None] < i, Mcol[:, None] * Y, 0.0), axis=0 

755 ) 

756 Yrow = (W1row - contrib) * (1.0 / Mii) 

757 Y = tl.where(col_idx[:, None] == i, Yrow[None, :], Y) 

758 Y = tl.where(col_idx[:, None] < ib, Y, 0.0) 

759 Yb = Yout + pid_b * sYb + pid_p * sYp 

760 tl.store(Yb + col_idx[:, None] * sYm + tn_idx[None, :] * sYn, Y) 

761 

762 

763@libentry() 

764@triton.jit 

765def _larfb_apply_kernel_mx( 

766 V, 

767 Y, 

768 C, 

769 M, 

770 ib, 

771 P, 

772 sVb, 

773 sVm, 

774 sVn, 

775 sYb, 

776 sYp, 

777 sYm, 

778 sYn, 

779 sCb, 

780 sCm, 

781 sCn, 

782 GRAN: tl.constexpr, 

783 IBN: tl.constexpr, 

784 TN: tl.constexpr, 

785 CH: tl.constexpr, 

786): 

787 """C[lo:hi, p-tile] -= V[lo:hi] Y, with Y precomputed per (batch, p-tile) 

788 by _larfb_solve_kernel_mx (rank-CH broadcast updates, dot-free).""" 

789 pid_b = tle.program_id(0) 

790 rid = tle.program_id(1) 

791 pid_p = tle.program_id(2) 

792 Vb = V + pid_b * sVb 

793 Cb = C + pid_b * sCb 

794 

795 col_idx = tl.arange(0, IBN) 

796 tn_idx = tl.arange(0, TN) 

797 p_idx = pid_p * TN + tn_idx 

798 pmask = p_idx < P 

799 lo = rid * GRAN 

800 hi = tl.minimum(lo + GRAN, M) 

801 

802 Yb = Y + pid_b * sYb + pid_p * sYp 

803 Yt = tl.load(Yb + col_idx[:, None] * sYm + tn_idx[None, :] * sYn) 

804 Yt = tl.where(col_idx[:, None] < ib, Yt, 0.0) 

805 

806 # ---- C[lo:hi, p-tile] -= V Y (rank-CH broadcast updates) ---- 

807 for t in range(0, (hi - lo + CH - 1) // CH): 

808 rows = lo + t * CH + tl.arange(0, CH) 

809 rmask = rows < hi 

810 v_off = rows[:, None] * sVm + col_idx[None, :] * sVn 

811 c_off = rows[:, None] * sCm + p_idx[None, :] * sCn 

812 Vc = tl.load( 

813 Vb + v_off, mask=rmask[:, None] & (col_idx[None, :] < ib), other=0.0 

814 ) 

815 Cc = tl.load(Cb + c_off, mask=rmask[:, None] & pmask[None, :], other=0.0) 

816 Cc = Cc - tl.sum(Vc[:, :, None] * Yt[None, :, :], axis=1) 

817 tl.store(Cb + c_off, Cc, mask=rmask[:, None] & pmask[None, :]) 

818 

819 

820# =========================================================================== 

821# T-fused variant of the generic _geqrt_sram_kernel (fp32 only): after the 

822# in-SRAM reflector chain the panel tile still holds every reflector tail, so 

823# the compact-WY factor T (INVERT form, identical math to _larft_kernel 

824# INVERT=True) is built in-register and stored with the panel -- removing one 

825# kernel launch + one global V re-read per panel. The launcher below feeds 

826# TBUF at the panel's (kk, kk) offset; callers must skip the separate larft 

827# launch for panels factorised here (see _panel_has_fused_t). 

828# =========================================================================== 

829@libentry() 

830@triton.jit 

831def _geqrt_sram_t_kernel_mx( 

832 W, 

833 V, 

834 TAU, 

835 TBUF, 

836 M, 

837 ib, 

838 kk, 

839 n, 

840 k, 

841 sWb, 

842 sWm, 

843 sWn, 

844 sVb, 

845 sVm, 

846 sVn, 

847 sTauB, 

848 sTauN, 

849 sTb, 

850 sTm, 

851 sTn, 

852 BM: tl.constexpr, 

853 IBN: tl.constexpr, 

854): 

855 pid = tle.program_id(0) 

856 Wb = W + pid * sWb 

857 Vb = V + pid * sVb 

858 TAUb = TAU + pid * sTauB 

859 dt = Wb.dtype.element_ty 

860 zero = tl.zeros((), dtype=dt) 

861 one = tl.full((), 1.0, dtype=dt) 

862 

863 rm = tl.arange(0, BM) # panel-local row (0..BM-1 -> rows kk..kk+M-1) 

864 cn = tl.arange(0, IBN) # panel-local col (0..IBN-1 -> cols kk..kk+IBN-1) 

865 rmask = rm < M 

866 cmask = cn < ib 

867 

868 # load the panel W[kk:kk+M, kk:kk+ib] into one SRAM tile 

869 rows_g = kk + rm 

870 cols_g = kk + cn 

871 A = tl.load( 

872 Wb + rows_g[:, None] * sWm + cols_g[None, :] * sWn, 

873 mask=rmask[:, None] & cmask[None, :], 

874 other=zero, 

875 ) 

876 

877 # tau accumulates in registers and is flushed with ONE vector store after 

878 # the loop -- 0-d scalar stores are unreliable on some vendor backends 

879 tau_arr = tl.zeros([IBN], dtype=dt) 

880 two = tl.arange(0, 2) 

881 for j in range(ib): 

882 col_j = tl.sum(tl.where(cn[None, :] == j, A, zero), axis=1) 

883 # alpha (row j) and the tail's squared norm in ONE cross-lane 

884 # reduction over the row axis: two dependent (BM,) reduction passes 

885 # become a single (BM, 2) pass, then two register-local extracts. 

886 pair = tl.sum( 

887 tl.join( 

888 tl.where(rm == j, col_j, zero), tl.where(rm > j, col_j * col_j, zero) 

889 ), 

890 axis=0, 

891 ) 

892 alpha = tl.sum(tl.where(two == 0, pair, zero)) 

893 xnorm_sq = tl.sum(tl.where(two == 1, pair, zero)) 

894 norm = tl.sqrt(alpha * alpha + xnorm_sq) 

895 beta = tl.where(alpha >= zero, -norm, norm) 

896 reflect = xnorm_sq > zero 

897 beta_eff = tl.where(reflect, beta, alpha) 

898 tau = tl.where(reflect, (beta - alpha) / beta, zero) 

899 denom = alpha - beta 

900 v_tail = tl.where(reflect, col_j / denom, zero) # guard 0/0 NaN 

901 # Householder vector vj (0/<j, 1/==j, tail/>j) 

902 vj = tl.where(rm > j, v_tail, tl.where(rm == j, one, zero)) 

903 vj = tl.where(reflect, vj, tl.where(rm == j, one, zero)) 

904 # write vj to the V buffer and the R/V values into the in-SRAM panel 

905 # (independent of the trailing reduction below -- issue it first) 

906 tl.store(Vb + rows_g * sVm + (kk + j) * sVn, vj, mask=rmask) 

907 # trailing update within the panel (cols j+1..ib), in SRAM 

908 pmask = cn[None, :] > j 

909 w = tau * tl.sum(tl.where(pmask, vj[:, None] * A, zero), axis=0) 

910 A = tl.where((rm[:, None] == j) & (cn[None, :] == j), beta_eff, A) 

911 A = tl.where((rm[:, None] > j) & (cn[None, :] == j), v_tail[:, None], A) 

912 # write tau 

913 tau_arr = tl.where(cn == j, tau, tau_arr) 

914 A = tl.where(pmask, A - vj[:, None] * w[None, :], A) 

915 

916 # flush tau with one vector store 

917 tl.store(TAUb + (kk + cn) * sTauN, tau_arr, mask=cmask) 

918 

919 # write the panel back to W (upper triangle holds R; strict-lower holds the 

920 # reflector tails, harmless -- _triu_copy only reads the upper triangle) 

921 tl.store( 

922 Wb + rows_g[:, None] * sWm + cols_g[None, :] * sWn, 

923 A, 

924 mask=rmask[:, None] & cmask[None, :], 

925 ) 

926 

927 # ---- fused DLARFT: T = (triu(V^H V, 1) + diag(1/tau))^{-1} ---- 

928 # V from the in-register tile: strict-lower tails + unit diagonal (columns 

929 # beyond ib stay zero, exactly like the explicit zeros in the V buffer). 

930 # BM >= 16 is guaranteed by the caller so the tl.dot K-dim is legal. 

931 Vt = tl.where(rm[:, None] > cn[None, :], A, zero) 

932 Vt = tl.where((rm[:, None] == cn[None, :]) & cmask[None, :], one, Vt) 

933 G = tl.dot(tl.trans(Vt), Vt, allow_tf32=False) 

934 # dinv = 1/M_ii = tau (resp. 0 for tau == 0): division-free, and the 

935 # zero-tau T row comes out exactly zero as in the generic kernel. 

936 U = tl.where(cn[:, None] < cn[None, :], G, zero) 

937 X = -U * tau_arr[:, None] # N = D^{-1} U: ROW scaling 

938 eye = tl.where(cn[:, None] == cn[None, :], one, zero) 

939 S = eye + X 

940 # Neumann product: X is strictly upper hence nilpotent (X^IBN == 0); 

941 # 5 squarings cover IBN <= 64, extra iterations are no-ops. 

942 for _ in range(5): 

943 X = tl.dot(X, X, allow_tf32=False) 

944 S = tl.dot(S, eye + X, allow_tf32=False) 

945 Tmat = S * tau_arr[None, :] # T = S D^{-1}: COLUMN scaling 

946 tl.store( 

947 TBUF + pid * sTb + (kk + cn)[:, None] * sTm + (kk + cn)[None, :] * sTn, 

948 Tmat, 

949 mask=cmask[:, None] & cmask[None, :], 

950 ) 

951 

952 

953def _launch_geqrt_sram_t_mx(W, V, tau, Tbuf, m, n, k, kk, ib, B): 

954 """SRAM-resident panel factorisation with fused T build (fp32 only).""" 

955 ib_active = min(ib, k - kk) 

956 M = m - kk 

957 sWb, sWm, sWn = W.stride() 

958 sVb, sVm, sVn = V.stride() 

959 sTauB, sTauN = tau.stride() 

960 sTb, sTm, sTn = Tbuf.stride() 

961 # .fn bypasses the libentry wrapper's per-launch key building (~10us on 

962 # this CPU); the bare @libentry() carries no tuning policy, so the raw 

963 # JITFunction launch is semantically identical. 

964 _geqrt_sram_t_kernel_mx.fn[(B,)]( 

965 W, 

966 V, 

967 tau, 

968 Tbuf, 

969 M, 

970 ib_active, 

971 kk, 

972 n, 

973 k, 

974 sWb, 

975 sWm, 

976 sWn, 

977 sVb, 

978 sVm, 

979 sVn, 

980 sTauB, 

981 sTauN, 

982 sTb, 

983 sTm, 

984 sTn, 

985 BM=triton.next_power_of_2(M), 

986 IBN=max(16, triton.next_power_of_2(ib_active)), 

987 num_warps=_GEQRT_SRAM_WARPS, 

988 ) 

989 

990 

991def _panel_has_fused_t(esz, m, kk, ib): 

992 """True when the panel at ``kk`` is factorised by the T-fused SRAM kernel 

993 (fp32, 16 <= pow2(M) <= sram cap) and its T tile is already in Tbuf -- 

994 callers must not run larft for it. ``bm >= 16`` keeps the fused kernel's 

995 tl.dot K-dim legal; smaller tail panels take the plain kernel + larft. 

996 """ 

997 if esz != 4: 

998 return False 

999 cap = _GEQRT_SRAM_MAX_M * _PANEL_IB // max(ib, _PANEL_IB) 

1000 bm = triton.next_power_of_2(m - kk) 

1001 return 16 <= bm <= cap 

1002 

1003 

1004def _launch_geqrt_mcta_mx(

1080# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

1081# metax launch wrappers: same contracts as the generic _launch_* helpers, but 

1082# routing fp64 to the dot-free broadcast kernels and fp32 to the generic ones. 

1083# Row-chunk width for the fp64 broadcast products: sized so the 3D broadcast 

1084# tile stays <= _BCAST_ELEM fp64 elements (8192 = 64 KB of registers per CTA 

1085# -- measured safe and ~6-8% faster than the original 4096 budget on the 

1086# blocked fp64 path; the larft Gram tile is (CH, IBN, IBN) so CH tops out at 

1087# 2 for IBN=64, larfb's (CH, IBN, TN) at CH=4). A fixed CH=4 at IBN=64 for 

1088# the Gram tile (128 KB) silently corrupts results -- never hard-code CH. 

1089# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

1090_BCAST_ELEM = 8192 

1091# fp64 larft/larfb row-chunk size for the row-parallel path (used when the 

1092# panel is taller than one chunk). Swept 16..2048 on (4096,4096)/(1024,1024) 

1093# fp64: 32-64 are the sweet spot (4096^2 r-mode 255 ms vs 320 at 512, vs 502 

1094# at 2048); 64 keeps a small edge on the largest shapes. 

1095_PAR_GRAN = 64 

1096 

1097# fp64 multi-CTA rows-per-CTA: 64 for very tall panels (fp64 4096^2 r-mode 

1098# 255 -> 245 ms) but the generic 32 below the gate -- at mid sizes the larger 

1099# per-CTA chunk's serial cost dominates (1024^2 fp64 reduced: 35.7 -> 43.4 ms 

1100# regression with an ungated 64). 

1101_MCTA_RM_FP64_BIG = 64 

1102_MCTA_FP64_BIG_M = 2048 

1103# fp32 multi-CTA panel rows-per-CTA for mid-size panels: 32 wins where the 

1104# barrier participants are few (1024^2 r-mode 10.1 -> 9.0 ms) but loses once 

1105# NC hits the 64-CTA cap (4096^2 r 71.7 -> 79.4 ms), so only panels with 

1106# M <= _MCTA_SMALL_M use it. 

1107_MCTA_RM_SMALL = 32 

1108_MCTA_SMALL_M = 2048 

1109# fp32 larfb narrow-trailing tile width (see _launch_larfb_mx). 

1110_LARFB_TN_SMALL = 16 

1111_LARFB_TN_SMALL_MAX_P = 1024 

1112 

1113 

1114def _bcast_ch(ibn, other): 

1115 return max(1, min(8, _BCAST_ELEM // (ibn * max(other, 1))))

1212 # wide ones (4096^2 reduced regresses 111 -> 121 ms), so gate on p.

1447# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

1448# metax-private tile caps (quirk #3). Unlike H20 (228 KB shared/CTA), this 

1449# backend has 64 KB shared and ~128 KB of private (register) tile budget per 

1450# CTA, and the two limits bite DIFFERENT kernels (measured on hardware): 

1451# * register-resident kernels (geqrt_sram, tsqr local/tree, qr_fused) never 

1452# touch shared meaningfully -- their real bound is the private budget 

1453# (BM*IBN*itemsize <= ~128 KB, numerically fine even at BM=1024). But on 

1454# this backend a BM=512 register-resident panel is ~1.5-2x SLOWER than the 

1455# multi-CTA factorisation (spill), so the cap stays small: 256 (measured 

1456# sweet spot; 64/128/256 tie, 512 clearly loses). 

1457# * the TSQR budgets (fp32 apply shared-bound to BM*IBN <= 8192; fp64 

1458# register-bound) are decoupled per dtype in _tsqr_mx below -- the single 

1459# generic constant cannot express both. 

1460# Wider fp64 panels (ib=64 vs the generic 32) halve the panel count -- and 

1461# with it the serial factor->T->trailing chain -- for a measured 7-15% win on 

1462# fp64 squares and wide-blocked inputs on this backend. fp32 keeps the 

1463# generic 32 (its dot path is fast enough that wider tiles just spill). 

1464# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

1465_GEQRT_SRAM_MAX_M = 256 

1466_PANEL_IB_FP64 = 64 

1467# r-mode-only fp32 panel width: with no Q to assemble, the cost is the serial 

1468# per-panel geqrt chain, whose per-reflector tile reductions scale with the 

1469# panel width. ib=16 measured ~16-21% faster than 32 on mid-size r-mode 

1470# squares (256^2/512^2/1024^2); it LOSES on 2048^2+ and on wide small-k 

1471# shapes, and for modes that assemble Q it would DOUBLE the number of 

1472# stream-ordered assembly sweeps (4096^2 fp32 109->140 ms) -- hence the 

1473# narrow gate below. 

1474_PANEL_IB_R_FP32 = 16 

1475 

1476 

1477def _r_mode_ib(esz, m, n, k, mode): 

1478 """Panel width for the blocked factorisation (None = dtype default).""" 

1479 if mode == "r" and esz == 4 and 128 <= k <= 1024 and n <= 1024: 

1480 return _PANEL_IB_R_FP32 

1481 return None 

1482 

1483 

1484def _blocked_qr_mx(W, V, tau, Tbuf, m, n, k, ib=None): 

1485 """In-place blocked Householder QR; leaves R in the upper triangle of W. 

1486 

1487 Same panel loop as the generic ``_blocked_qr``, but the compact-WY 

1488 build/apply go through the metax launch wrappers (fp64 dot-free kernels; 

1489 fp32 larfb at a pinned num_stages=1) and the SRAM cap uses the 

1490 metax-calibrated value. fp64 panels are widened to ib=64 (see above); 

1491 the factorisation and Q assembly below stay in sync on the panel width. 

1492 """ 

1493 if W.element_size() == 8: 

1494 ib = _PANEL_IB_FP64 

1495 elif ib is None: 

1496 ib = _PANEL_IB 

1497 B = W.shape[0] 

1498 P = (k + ib - 1) // ib 

1499 dt = W.dtype 

1500 dev = W.device 

1501 # The SRAM kernel keeps both the A tile and V_panel live; fp64 doubles 

1502 # register pressure and never wins on this backend -> disable it there. 

1503 sram_max_m = _GEQRT_SRAM_MAX_M if W.element_size() == 4 else 0 

1504 # the SRAM kernel keeps a (BM, IBN) register tile: wider panels (ib=64) 

1505 # double its size, so halve the row cap to stay out of the spill regime. 

1506 # NOTE: the cap is pinned at _GEQRT_SRAM_MAX_M for ib < _PANEL_IB on 

1507 # purpose -- BM=512 single-CTA panels measure 1.5-2x SLOWER than the 

1508 # multi-CTA path even at half the tile bytes (512x16 fp32), so a 

1509 # tile-byte-based cap was tried and reverted. 

1510 sram_max_m = sram_max_m * _PANEL_IB // max(ib, _PANEL_IB) 

1511 # multi-CTA scratch (one slot per (panel, column), used once -> zeroed once); 

1512 # allocated only when at least one panel actually takes the multi-CTA path. 

1513 needs_mcta = any( 

1514 triton.next_power_of_2(m - kk) > sram_max_m for kk in range(0, k, ib) 

1515 ) 

1516 if needs_mcta: 

1517 alpha_buf = torch.zeros(B, P, ib, dtype=dt, device=dev) 

1518 xnorm_buf = torch.zeros(B, P, ib, dtype=dt, device=dev) 

1519 w_sum = torch.zeros(B, P, ib, ib, dtype=dt, device=dev) 

1520 rowj_buf = torch.zeros(B, P, ib, ib, dtype=dt, device=dev) 

1521 ctr = torch.zeros(B, P, ib, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev) 

1522 # Hoisted stride tuples + as_strided views: plain getitem slicing costs 

1523 # ~4us per view on this host CPU and the loop below runs k/ib panels per 

1524 # call, which is the CPU-bound regime for small/mid squares. 

1525 sW = W.stride() 

1526 sV = V.stride() 

1527 sTau = tau.stride() 

1528 sTb_, sTm_, sTn_ = Tbuf.stride() 

1529 soW, soV, soTau, soTb = (t.storage_offset() for t in (W, V, tau, Tbuf)) 

1530 for kk in range(0, k, ib): 

1531 ib_active = min(ib, k - kk) 

1532 M = m - kk 

1533 bm = triton.next_power_of_2(M) 

1534 fused_t = False 

1535 if _panel_has_fused_t(W.element_size(), m, kk, ib): 

1536 # SRAM-resident factorisation with the WY factor T built in-kernel 

1537 # (fp32): saves one larft launch + one global V re-read per panel. 

1538 _launch_geqrt_sram_t_mx(W, V, tau, Tbuf, m, n, k, kk, ib_active, B) 

1539 fused_t = True 

1540 elif bm <= sram_max_m: 

1541 # panel fits SRAM: single-CTA resident factorisation (no global re-reads) 

1542 _launch_geqrt_sram(W, V, tau, m, k, kk, ib_active, B) 

1543 else: 

1544 # ceil(M/rm) CTAs -> CHUNK == rm -> the register-resident 

1545 # fast path of _geqrt_mcta_kernel (each CTA loads its row chunk 

1546 # once, no per-reflector global re-reads). 

1547 rm = _MCTA_RM if W.element_size() == 4 else _MCTA_RM_FP64 

1548 if W.element_size() == 4: 

1549 if M <= _MCTA_SMALL_M: 

1550 rm = _MCTA_RM_SMALL 

1551 elif M > _MCTA_FP64_BIG_M: 

1552 rm = _MCTA_RM_FP64_BIG 

1553 nc = max(1, min(_MCTA_NC_MAX, (M + rm - 1) // rm)) 

1554 if nc >= _MCTA_MIN_NC: 

1555 _launch_geqrt_mcta_mx( 

1556 W, 

1557 V, 

1558 tau, 

1559 alpha_buf, 

1560 xnorm_buf, 

1561 w_sum, 

1562 rowj_buf, 

1563 ctr, 

1564 m, 

1565 k, 

1566 kk, 

1567 ib_active, 

1568 kk // ib, 

1569 nc, 

1570 B, 

1571 rm=rm, 

1572 ) 

1573 else: 

1574 _launch_geqrt(W, V, tau, m, k, kk, ib_active, B) 

1575 Vp = torch.as_strided(V, (B, M, ib_active), sV, soV + kk * sV[1] + kk * sV[2]) 

1576 taup = torch.as_strided(tau, (B, ib_active), sTau, soTau + kk * sTau[1]) 

1577 Tp = torch.as_strided( 

1578 Tbuf, 

1579 (B, ib_active, ib_active), 

1580 (sTb_, sTm_, sTn_), 

1581 soTb + kk * sTm_ + kk * sTn_, 

1582 ) 

1583 if kk + ib_active < n: 

1584 if not fused_t: 

1585 _launch_larft_mx(Vp, taup, Tp, m, kk, ib_active, B) 

1586 C = torch.as_strided( 

1587 W, 

1588 (B, M, n - (kk + ib_active)), 

1589 sW, 

1590 soW + kk * sW[1] + (kk + ib_active) * sW[2], 

1591 ) 

1592 _launch_larfb_mx( 

1593 Vp, Tp, C, m - kk, n - (kk + ib_active), ib_active, B, upper=False 

1594 ) 

1595 

1596 

1597# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

1598# metax-private TSQR orchestration. Same algorithm / phases as the generic 

1599# _tsqr, but the register/shared budgets are decoupled per dtype (the generic 

1600# code derives both from one fp32 constant divided by 4 for fp64, which on 

1601# this backend cripples the fp64 routing): 

1602# 

1603# * fp64 local/apply tiles are REGISTER-bound and tolerate spill (measured 

1604# correct up to 512x64), so the row block can be 128 rows -- halving the 

1605# block count vs the generic fp64 routing. The generic budget (2048 

1606# elements after the /4) gives br = 65 at n = 64, i.e. 2x the blocks and 

1607# a tree stack that no longer fits the two-level budget -> every tall 

1608# fp64 input fell back to the (slow) blocked path. 

1609# * fp64 tree tiles are hard-limited to 32768 elements by private memory 

1610# (1024x64 fails to launch), fp32 to 65536. 

1611# * fp32 row blocks stay bounded by the APPLY kernel's shared memory 

1612# (BM*IBN <= 8192), as in the generic code. 

1613# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

1614_TSQR_MX_BR_FP64 = 128 # fp64 row-block cap (swept: 64/128/256 -> 128 wins 

1615# # on every tall-skinny fp64 shape; 256's spill 

1616# # costs more than the halved block count saves) 

1617_TSQR_MX_LOCAL_FP64 = 16384 # fp64 local-tile element budget 

1618_TSQR_MX_RED_FP64 = 32768 # fp64 tree-tile element budget (private mem wall) 

1619_TSQR_MX_LOCAL_FP32 = 8192 # fp32: bounded by the apply kernel's shared mem 

1620_TSQR_MX_RED_FP32 = 65536 # fp32 tree-tile budget (two-level group/top tiles) 

1621# A flat reduction is ONE CTA factoring the whole stack serially -- profitable 

1622# only while the stack is small; past that the two-level tree (parallel group 

1623# reductions) wins despite the extra launch. Measured on this backend: the 

1624# crossover is ~16K fp32 elements (e.g. 2048x64 fp32: flat 24 ms vs two-level 

1625# ~7 ms). fp64 keeps the generic BRM <= _TSQR_TREE_FLAT_ROWS rule. 

1626_TSQR_MX_FLAT_FP32 = 16384 

1627 

1628 

1629def _tsqr_mx(W, m, n, k, mode, B, out_Q=None, out_R=None): 

1630 """Returns (Q or None, R). R is (B, n, n); Q (reduced) is (B, m, n).""" 

1631 dt = W.dtype 

1632 dev = W.device 

1633 IBN = max(16, triton.next_power_of_2(n)) 

1634 sWb, sWm, sWn = W.stride() 

1635 esz = W.element_size() 

1636 if esz == 8: 

1637 sram_elem = _TSQR_MX_LOCAL_FP64 

1638 red_elem = _TSQR_MX_RED_FP64 

1639 fin_br = _TSQR_MX_BR_FP64 

1640 else: 

1641 sram_elem = _TSQR_MX_LOCAL_FP32 

1642 red_elem = _TSQR_MX_RED_FP32 

1643 fin_br = _TSQR_BR 

1644 write_Q = mode != "r" 

1645 

1646 # Row-block size: the local kernel keeps a (pow2(br), IBN) register tile. 

1647 # Every block must hold >= n+1 rows (a shorter block could not produce n 

1648 # orthonormal local Q columns), so rebalance until the last block does. 

1649 br = max(n + 1, min(m, fin_br, sram_elem // n)) 

1650 num_blocks = (m + br - 1) // br 

1651 while num_blocks > 1 and m - (num_blocks - 1) * br < n + 1: 

1652 num_blocks -= 1 

1653 br = max(n + 1, (m + num_blocks - 1) // num_blocks) 

1654 Rm = num_blocks * n 

1655 

1656 R_blocks = torch.empty(B, num_blocks, n, n, dtype=dt, device=dev) 

1657 Racc = out_R if out_R is not None else torch.empty(B, n, n, dtype=dt, device=dev) 

1658 

1659 IBNt = triton.next_power_of_2(n) 

1660 BRM = triton.next_power_of_2(Rm) 

1661 flat = ( 

1662 BRM * IBNt <= red_elem 

1663 and BRM * IBNt <= _TSQR_MX_FLAT_FP32 

1664 and (esz == 4 or BRM <= _TSQR_TREE_FLAT_ROWS) 

1665 ) 

1666 grp = num_blocks 

1667 num_groups = 1 

1668 if not flat: 

1669 cap = max(1, red_elem // (IBNt * IBNt)) # group-tile budget, in blocks 

1670 cap = 1 << (cap.bit_length() - 1) # round down to a power of two 

1671 g = 1 

1672 while g * g < num_blocks: 

1673 g <<= 1 

1674 grp = min(g, cap) 

1675 num_groups = (num_blocks + grp - 1) // grp 

1676 while ( 

1677 grp < num_blocks 

1678 and triton.next_power_of_2(num_groups * n) * IBNt > red_elem 

1679 ): 

1680 grp <<= 1 

1681 num_groups = (num_blocks + grp - 1) // grp 

1682 two_level = ( 

1683 num_groups > 1 

1684 and grp <= cap 

1685 and triton.next_power_of_2(num_groups * n) * IBNt <= red_elem 

1686 ) 

1687 else: 

1688 two_level = False 

1689 use_tree = flat or two_level 

1690 # fold the tree reduction into the apply kernel for small fp32 stacks 

1691 BRMt = max(16, triton.next_power_of_2(Rm)) 

1692 fold = flat and write_Q and esz == 4 and BRMt * IBN <= _TSQR_FOLD_ELEM 

1693 

1694 if write_Q: 

1695 Q = out_Q if out_Q is not None else torch.empty(B, m, n, dtype=dt, device=dev) 

1696 V_local = torch.empty(B, m, n, dtype=dt, device=dev) 

1697 TAU_local = torch.empty(B, num_blocks, n, dtype=dt, device=dev) 

1698 Qt = Racc if fold else torch.empty(B, Rm, n, dtype=dt, device=dev) 

1699 Qt2 = ( 

1700 torch.empty(B, num_groups * n, n, dtype=dt, device=dev) if two_level else Qt 

1701 ) 

1702 else: 

1703 # dummy pointers, never read or written (STORE_V / write_Q are False) 

1704 Q = Qt = Qt2 = V_local = TAU_local = torch.empty(B, 1, 1, dtype=dt, device=dev) 

1705 

1706 # ---- Phase 1: local QR of all row blocks in one launch ---- 

1707 k_max = min(br, n) 

1708 BM = triton.next_power_of_2(br) 

1709 sVb, sVm, sVn = V_local.stride() 

1710 _tsqr_local_sram_kernel[(B, num_blocks)]( 

1711 W, 

1712 R_blocks, 

1713 V_local, 

1714 TAU_local, 

1715 m, 

1716 n, 

1717 br, 

1718 num_blocks, 

1719 k_max, 

1720 sWb, 

1721 sWm, 

1722 sWn, 

1723 R_blocks.stride(0), 

1724 R_blocks.stride(1), 

1725 R_blocks.stride(2), 

1726 sVb, 

1727 sVm, 

1728 sVn, 

1729 TAU_local.stride(0), 

1730 BM=BM, 

1731 IBN=IBN, 

1732 STORE_V=write_Q, 

1733 num_warps=max(4, min(16, (BM * IBN) // 4096)), 

1734 ) 

1735 

1736 # ---- Phase 2: tree reduction of the stacked local R factors ---- 

1737 def tree_warps(tile_rows): 

1738 return _TSQR_TREE_WARPS if tile_rows * IBNt * esz <= 16384 else 8 

1739 

1740 if use_tree: 

1741 if fold: 

1742 pass # the apply kernel factors the stack redundantly per CTA 

1743 elif two_level: 

1744 Rg = torch.empty(B, num_groups, n, n, dtype=dt, device=dev) 

1745 _tsqr_tree_kernel[(B, num_groups)]( 

1746 R_blocks, 

1747 Rg, 

1748 Qt, 

1749 n, 

1750 num_blocks, 

1751 grp, 

1752 write_Q, 

1753 Rg.stride(0), 

1754 Rg.stride(2), 

1755 Rg.stride(3), 

1756 BRM=grp * IBNt, 

1757 IBN=IBNt, 

1758 num_warps=tree_warps(grp * IBNt), 

1759 ) 

1760 BRMt2 = triton.next_power_of_2(num_groups * n) 

1761 _tsqr_tree_kernel[(B, 1)]( 

1762 Rg, 

1763 Racc, 

1764 Qt2, 

1765 n, 

1766 num_groups, 

1767 num_groups, 

1768 write_Q, 

1769 Racc.stride(0), 

1770 Racc.stride(1), 

1771 Racc.stride(2), 

1772 BRM=BRMt2, 

1773 IBN=IBNt, 

1774 num_warps=tree_warps(BRMt2), 

1775 ) 

1776 else: 

1777 # stack fits one register-resident CTA per batch: factor + build Q_t 

1778 _tsqr_tree_kernel[(B, 1)]( 

1779 R_blocks, 

1780 Racc, 

1781 Qt, 

1782 n, 

1783 num_blocks, 

1784 num_blocks, 

1785 write_Q, 

1786 Racc.stride(0), 

1787 Racc.stride(1), 

1788 Racc.stride(2), 

1789 BRM=BRM, 

1790 IBN=IBNt, 

1791 num_warps=tree_warps(BRM), 

1792 ) 

1793 else: 

1794 # Stack too tall even for a two-level tree: factor it with the blocked 

1795 # path and assemble Q_t from its reflectors (the metax launch wrappers 

1796 # and stream-ordered assembly are used automatically). 

1797 Rstack = R_blocks.reshape(B, Rm, n) 

1798 Vt = ( 

1799 torch.zeros(B, Rm, n, dtype=dt, device=dev) 

1800 if write_Q 

1801 else torch.empty(B, Rm, n, dtype=dt, device=dev) 

1802 ) 

1803 tau_t = torch.empty(B, n, dtype=dt, device=dev) 

1804 Tbuf_t = torch.empty(B, n, n, dtype=dt, device=dev) 

1805 _blocked_qr_mx(Rstack, Vt, tau_t, Tbuf_t, Rm, n, n) 

1806 _triu_copy(Rstack, Racc, n, n, B) 

1807 if write_Q: 

1808 _assemble_q_mx(Vt, tau_t, Tbuf_t, Rm, n, n, n, _PANEL_IB, B, Qt) 

1809 two_level = False 

1810 

1811 if not write_Q: 

1812 return None, Racc 

1813 

1814 # ---- Phase 3: Q[block rows] = Q_local @ Q_t[block rows], one CTA/block ---- 

1815 _launch_tsqr_apply( 

1816 (B, num_blocks), 

1817 V_local, 

1818 TAU_local, 

1819 Qt, 

1820 Qt2, 

1821 Q, 

1822 R_blocks, 

1823 Racc, 

1824 m, 

1825 n, 

1826 br, 

1827 k_max, 

1828 grp, 

1829 num_blocks, 

1830 Q.stride(0), 

1831 Q.stride(1), 

1832 Q.stride(2), 

1833 Racc.stride(0), 

1834 Racc.stride(1), 

1835 Racc.stride(2), 

1836 BM=BM, 

1837 IBN=IBN, 

1838 TWO_LEVEL=two_level, 

1839 FOLD_TREE=fold, 

1840 BRMt=BRMt if fold else 16, 

1841 num_warps=max(4, min(16, (BM * IBN) // 4096)), 

1842 ) 

1843 return Q, Racc 

1844 

1845 

1846def _assemble_q_mx(V, tau, Tbuf, m, n, k, qcols, ib, B, out): 

1847 """Stream-ordered Q assembly (quirk #2). 

1848 

1849 identity kernel + one larfb launch per panel (reverse order), so every 

1850 cross-panel dependency is ordered by the stream instead of an intra-kernel 

1851 global write->read. Uses the metax larft/larfb wrappers, so fp64 also 

1852 gets the dot-free kernels. The panel width is overridden for fp64 so it 

1853 always matches _blocked_qr_mx's factorisation. 

1854 """ 

1855 if V.element_size() == 8: 

1856 ib = _PANEL_IB_FP64 

1857 P = (k + ib - 1) // ib 

1858 kk_last = (P - 1) * ib 

1859 ib_last = min(ib, k - kk_last) 

1860 if kk_last + ib_last >= n and not _panel_has_fused_t( 

1861 V.element_size(), m, kk_last, ib 

1862 ): 

1863 # the last panel never got a T from _blocked_qr_mx (no trailing update) 

1864 # unless the T-fused SRAM kernel already wrote it 

1865 Vp = V[:, kk_last:m, kk_last : kk_last + ib_last] 

1866 taup = tau[:, kk_last : kk_last + ib_last] 

1867 Tp = Tbuf[:, kk_last : kk_last + ib_last, kk_last : kk_last + ib_last] 

1868 _launch_larft_mx(Vp, taup, Tp, m, kk_last, ib_last, B) 

1869 sQb, sQm, sQn = out.stride() 

1870 if P == 1 and (V.element_size() == 4 or (k <= _ASSEMBLE_1P_MAX_K_FP64 and m >= n)): 

1871 # single panel: Q = I - V T V^H in one pass -- W1 = T V[p,:]^H read 

1872 # straight off V's rows (no identity write + no Q re-reads). fp32 

1873 # uses the generic kernel (fp32 tl.dot is exact here); fp64 uses the 

1874 # dot-free row-parallel metax variant for tall/square shapes -- for 

1875 # wide ones (m < n, tiny square Q) the stream-ordered larfb is as 

1876 # fast and the redundant per-CTA W1 solve just adds launches. 

1877 Vp = V[:, :, :k] 

1878 Tp = Tbuf[:, :k, :k] 

1879 sVb, sVm, sVn = Vp.stride() 

1880 sTb, sTm, sTn = Tp.stride() 

1881 ibn = max(16, triton.next_power_of_2(k)) 

1882 grid_p = (qcols + _ASSEMBLE_TN - 1) // _ASSEMBLE_TN 

1883 if V.element_size() == 4: 

1884 _assemble_q_single_panel_kernel[(B, grid_p)]( 

1885 Vp, 

1886 Tp, 

1887 out, 

1888 m, 

1889 k, 

1890 qcols, 

1891 sVb, 

1892 sVm, 

1893 sVn, 

1894 sTb, 

1895 sTm, 

1896 sTn, 

1897 sQb, 

1898 sQm, 

1899 sQn, 

1900 RM=_ASSEMBLE_RM, 

1901 TN=_ASSEMBLE_TN, 

1902 IBN=ibn, 

1903 num_warps=_ASSEMBLE_WARPS, 

1904 ) 

1905 else: 

1906 grid_r = (m + _ASSEMBLE_RM - 1) // _ASSEMBLE_RM 

1907 _assemble_q_single_panel_kernel_mx[(B, grid_r, grid_p)]( 

1908 Vp, 

1909 Tp, 

1910 out, 

1911 m, 

1912 k, 

1913 qcols, 

1914 sVb, 

1915 sVm, 

1916 sVn, 

1917 sTb, 

1918 sTm, 

1919 sTn, 

1920 sQb, 

1921 sQm, 

1922 sQn, 

1923 RM=_ASSEMBLE_RM, 

1924 TN=_ASSEMBLE_TN, 

1925 IBN=ibn, 

1926 num_warps=_ASSEMBLE_WARPS, 

1927 ) 

1928 return out 

1929 grid_e = (m * qcols + 1023) // 1024 

1930 _identity_kernel[(B * grid_e,)](out, m, qcols, grid_e, sQb, sQm, sQn, BLOCK=1024) 

1931 for kk in reversed(range(0, k, ib)): 

1932 ib_active = min(ib, k - kk) 

1933 Vp = V[:, kk:m, kk : kk + ib_active] 

1934 Tp = Tbuf[:, kk : kk + ib_active, kk : kk + ib_active] 

1935 _launch_larfb_mx( 

1936 Vp, Tp, out[:, kk:m, :], m - kk, qcols, ib_active, B, upper=True 

1937 ) 

1938 return out 

1939 

1940 

1941# fp64 single-panel one-pass assembly gate (see _assemble_q_mx): row-parallel 

1942# one-pass wins for tall/square panels up to k=64 on this backend. 

1943_ASSEMBLE_1P_MAX_K_FP64 = 64 

1944 

1945 

1946# =========================================================================== 

1947# Public op. Mirrors the generic _linalg_qr routing with the metax variants 

1948# plugged in (fused path and helpers are reused unchanged). 

1949# =========================================================================== 

1950def _linalg_qr_mx(A, mode="reduced", *, out=None): 

1951 _validate_mode(mode) 

1952 

1953 if A.dim() < 2: 

1954 raise RuntimeError("linalg_qr: input must have at least 2 dimensions") 

1955 if A.dtype not in (torch.float32, torch.float64): 

1956 raise NotImplementedError( 

1957 "FlagGems linalg_qr currently supports float32 and float64 inputs; " 

1958 f"got dtype={A.dtype}" 

1959 ) 

1960 

1961 orig_dtype = A.dtype 

1962 batch_shape = A.shape[:-2] 

1963 m, n = A.shape[-2], A.shape[-1] 

1964 k = min(m, n) 

1965 B = 1 

1966 for d in batch_shape: 

1967 B *= d 

1968 

1969 if out is not None: 

1970 _validate_out(out, A.dtype, batch_shape, m, n, mode) 

1971 

1972 if m == 0 or n == 0: 

1973 # Degenerate input: no factorisation to run. torch.linalg.qr returns 

1974 # empty factors, except complete mode with zero columns where Q = I. 

1975 if mode == "r": 

1976 q_shape, r_shape = (0,), (*batch_shape, k, n) 

1977 elif mode == "reduced": 

1978 q_shape, r_shape = (*batch_shape, m, k), (*batch_shape, k, n) 

1979 else: 

1980 q_shape, r_shape = (*batch_shape, m, m), (*batch_shape, m, n) 

1981 if out is not None: 

1982 Q, R = out 

1983 else: 

1984 Q = A.new_empty(q_shape) 

1985 R = A.new_empty(r_shape) 

1986 if mode == "complete" and n == 0 and m > 0: 

1987 eye = torch.eye(m, dtype=A.dtype, device=A.device) 

1988 Q.copy_(eye.expand(*batch_shape, m, m)) 

1989 return Q, R 

1990 

1991 # Read-only view of A. The fused and TSQR paths only read W (no copy 

1992 # needed); the blocked path factors in place and clones below. 

1993 W = A.reshape(B, m, n) 

1994 

1995 qcols = 0 if mode == "r" else (k if mode == "reduced" else m) 

1996 rrows = k if mode in ("reduced", "r") else m 

1997 # Resolve caller-provided output buffers (reshaped to the (B, ...) layout the 

1998 # kernels write). These are views of the user's tensors for the contiguous 

1999 # case, so the kernels write the user's memory directly -- no alloc/copy. 

2000 out_Q = out_R = None 

2001 if out is not None: 

2002 out_Q, out_R = out 

2003 out_Q = out_Q.reshape(B, m, qcols) if qcols else out_Q.reshape(0) 

2004 out_R = out_R.reshape(B, rrows, n) 

2005 # TSQR only for tall-skinny that fused can't fit (m*n > _FUSED_ELEM or m > _FUSED_M); 

2006 # smaller tall-skinny (e.g. 64×16, 128×32) are faster via the single-launch fused kernel. 

2007 # TSQR also needs m >= _TSQR_MIN_M -- below that the blocked path's zero-sync SRAM 

2008 # panels beat TSQR's per-block serial reflector chains (e.g. 512x64, 256x64). 

2009 is_ts = ( 

2010 (m >= _TSQR_ASPECT * n) 

2011 and (m >= _TSQR_MIN_M) 

2012 and (n > 0) 

2013 and (n <= _TSQR_MAX_N) 

2014 and (mode in ("reduced", "r")) 

2015 ) 

2016 # _FUSED_ELEM is calibrated for fp32; fp64 doubles register pressure in the 

2017 # fused kernel (A tile + Q tile both live during Q assembly), so larger fp64 

2018 # matrices spill and run ~2x slower than the blocked path (e.g. 64x64 fp64: 

2019 # fused 1120us vs blocked 581us). Cut the cap to ~1/4 for fp64 -- small / 

2020 # batched matrices stay fused (single launch wins), only the larger singles 

2021 # divert to blocked. 

2022 fused_elem = _FUSED_ELEM if A.element_size() == 4 else _FUSED_ELEM // 4 

2023 fits_fused = ( 

2024 m <= _FUSED_M 

2025 and n <= _FUSED_DIM 

2026 and m * n <= fused_elem 

2027 and (mode == "r" or qcols * m <= fused_elem) 

2028 ) 

2029 if is_ts: 

2030 fits_fused = fits_fused and (m <= _FUSED_TALL_M) 

2031 if fits_fused: 

2032 return _fused_qr(W, A, orig_dtype, batch_shape, m, n, k, mode, B, out_Q, out_R) 

2033 

2034 # large matrices: TSQR for tall-skinny, blocked Householder otherwise. 

2035 if is_ts: 

2036 Qm, Rm = _tsqr_mx(W, m, n, k, mode, B, out_Q, out_R) 

2037 if mode == "r": 

2038 return ( 

2039 out_Q if out_Q is not None else A.new_empty(0), 

2040 Rm.reshape(*batch_shape, n, n), 

2041 ) 

2042 return (Qm.reshape(*batch_shape, m, n), Rm.reshape(*batch_shape, n, n)) 

2043 

2044 # blocked Householder path (large matrices): kernels write W in place. 

2045 # V is zero-initialised when Q is assembled (mode != "r"): the paired 

2046 # assembly reads the whole trapezoid of V below each pair start, including 

2047 # entries above each reflector's diagonal that geqrt never writes -- 

2048 # mathematically zero, physically stale memory otherwise. tau/Tbuf are 

2049 # fully written by the geqrt/larft kernels before they are read (empty). 

2050 V = ( 

2051 torch.zeros(B, m, k, dtype=W.dtype, device=W.device) 

2052 if mode != "r" 

2053 else torch.empty(B, m, k, dtype=W.dtype, device=W.device) 

2054 ) 

2055 tau = torch.empty(B, k, dtype=W.dtype, device=W.device) 

2056 Tbuf = torch.empty(B, k, k, dtype=W.dtype, device=W.device) 

2057 W = W.clone() 

2058 ib = _r_mode_ib(W.element_size(), m, n, k, mode) 

2059 _blocked_qr_mx(W, V, tau, Tbuf, m, n, k, ib) 

2060 

2061 if mode == "r": 

2062 R = ( 

2063 out_R 

2064 if out_R is not None 

2065 else torch.empty(B, k, n, dtype=W.dtype, device=W.device) 

2066 ) 

2067 _triu_copy(W, R, k, n, B) 

2068 return ( 

2069 out_Q if out_Q is not None else A.new_empty(0), 

2070 R.reshape(*batch_shape, k, n), 

2071 ) 

2072 

2073 Q = ( 

2074 out_Q 

2075 if out_Q is not None 

2076 else torch.empty(B, m, qcols, dtype=W.dtype, device=W.device) 

2077 ) 

2078 _assemble_q_mx(V, tau, Tbuf, m, n, k, qcols, _PANEL_IB, B, Q) 

2079 

2080 R = ( 

2081 out_R 

2082 if out_R is not None 

2083 else torch.empty( 

2084 B, qcols if mode == "complete" else k, n, dtype=W.dtype, device=W.device 

2085 ) 

2086 ) 

2087 _triu_copy(W, R, R.shape[-2], n, B) 

2088 

2089 if mode == "reduced": 

2090 return (Q.reshape(*batch_shape, m, k), R.reshape(*batch_shape, k, n)) 

2091 return (Q.reshape(*batch_shape, m, m), R.reshape(*batch_shape, m, n)) 

2092 

2093 

2094def linalg_qr(A, mode="reduced", *, out=None): 

2095 logger.debug("GEMS_METAX LINALG_QR") 

2096 return _linalg_qr_mx(A, mode, out=out) 

2097 

2098 

2099def linalg_qr_out(A, mode="reduced", *, Q, R):
